extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate/graduate students and scholars of journalism and media studies; journalists and editors interested in news values
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes Conboy's criteria for what makes events or topics newsworthy in tabloid and broadsheet journalism, and his higher-level claims about how news values vary across time, format, and culture. Useful for analyzing or producing news that fits tabloid or broadsheet value-systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabloid as value system (not just format)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tabloid" extends beyond format — refers to news values regardless of page size
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conboy emphasizes that tabloid describes a set of news values (e.g., populism, sensationalism) that can appear in various formats, not only small-page tabloids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Populism (tabloid value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Populism — a core tabloid news value listed by Conboy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News framed as speaking for 'the people' or appealing to popular sentiment rather than elite perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility (tabloid value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility — a tabloid news value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for stories and language that are easy for general audiences to understand; low barrier to engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity (tabloid value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplicity — a tabloid news value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor straightforward, easily grasped narratives over complex, technical explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization (tabloid value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalization — a tabloid news value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on individuals, personalities and human-interest angles rather than abstract institutions or processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensationalism (tabloid value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensationalism — a tabloid news value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of shocking, attention-grabbing details and tone to attract readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drama / spectacle (tabloid value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drama / spectacle — a tabloid news value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories presented as dramatic events or spectacles, privileging spectacle over measured analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity (tabloid value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarity — a tabloid news value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for topics, narratives, and frames that feel familiar and reassuring to the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working-class identification (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working-class identification — content that 'speaks to "us"' (a tabloid criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames stories to align with working-class perspectives and identities; positions audience as the in-group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-elite stance (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-elite stance — punches up (tabloid criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories emphasize distrust of elites and institutions; narratives that challenge or ridicule powerful actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional immediacy (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional immediacy — 'feel before think' (tabloid criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritizes emotional reactions and visceral appeal over deliberative or analytical engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual prominence (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual prominence — large photos, headlines (tabloid criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and layout choices (big images, bold headlines) used to amplify story salience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrity centrality (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrity centrality — celebrities occupy central role in news selection (tabloid criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories focus on famous individuals and their lives as a key draw for audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex and scandal prominence (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex and scandal — prominent subject matter for tabloids
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage foregrounds sexual stories and scandals to attract attention and moral interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime and punishment drama (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crime and punishment — dramatized narratives of wrongdoing (tabloid criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on criminal acts, investigations, and punitive outcomes presented as moral drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underdog narratives (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Underdog narratives — favoring stories about overlooked or disadvantaged figures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames that present people or groups as struggling against powerful forces, eliciting sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patriotic appeal (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patriotic appeal — nationalistic framing as a tabloid criterion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that invoke national pride or use patriotic sentiments to mobilize readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common-sense framing (tabloid newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common-sense framing — simplifying complex issues into everyday terms (tabloid criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents issues through intuitive, familiar explanations rather than technical or expert discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-policy substance (broadsheet newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public-policy substance — broadsheet criterion emphasizing policy relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of stories with clear implications for public policy and democratic governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional accountability (broadsheet newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional accountability — holding institutions to account (broadsheet criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative or reporting work that scrutinizes institutions and their practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical depth (broadsheet newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical depth — emphasis on in-depth explanation and analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that explore causes, context, and implications rather than surface-level reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign affairs (broadsheet newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign affairs — international coverage prioritized by broadsheets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to global events, diplomacy, and international relations as newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business / economy (broadsheet newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Business/economy — economic reporting as broadsheet priority
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage of markets, macro- and micro-economic trends, and business implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural commentary (broadsheet newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural commentary — critique and interpretation of cultural life
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion, review, and interpretive pieces that contextualize culture and arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form investigation (broadsheet newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-form investigation — extended investigative reporting as broadsheet strength
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for lengthy, resource-intensive investigations that reveal systemic problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity tolerance (broadsheet newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complexity tolerance — willingness to present and tolerate complex, nuanced stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience and editorial norms that accept multifaceted explanations and ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values vary by era (meta-rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: News values vary by era — what's newsworthy in 1850 vs. 1950 vs. 2025
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conboy stresses historical contingency: evaluators should account for changing norms and contexts when assessing newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values vary by format (meta-rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: News values vary by format — broadsheet, tabloid, digital, broadcast influence selection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different media formats privilege different kinds of stories and presentation styles; analysts should factor format in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values vary by culture (meta-rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: News values vary by culture — UK, US, Global South differences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural context shapes what is considered important or interesting; avoid assuming universal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values are contested (meta-rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: News values are contested — they are constructed, not natural
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize debates and power dynamics that determine which values dominate; assessment should account for contention and perspective.
